sources.title: How to write your personal statement: 2026 entry onwards (UCAS)
sources.governs: All UCAS statements (main and, by Durham's rule, the substitute)
sources.notes: Defines the three questions, 350 minimum per answer, 4000 total including spaces. Q1 guidance mentions future plans, which disagrees with LSE's Q1 rule (see lse-ps).
extracts: the personal statement will still be 4000 characters in total; this includes spaces
Each section will have a minimum character count of 350 characters
admissions staff will review the three questions as a whole
Q1: motivations, your knowledge of the subject, and your future plans ... universities and colleges want to see you've done your research
Q2: most recent and relevant study ... universities and colleges will see students' grades elsewhere on their application, so don't waste time talking about these
Q3: work, volunteering, personal experiences, hobbies ... reflecting on why each one is useful
each part of the statement should add value ... not to repeat information

sources.title: A guide to using AI and ChatGPT with your personal statement (UCAS)
sources.notes: Permits AI for ideas, structure, readability; forbids submitting AI text. Contains the declaration wording. An older UCAS builder page says not to use AI at all (ucas-builder-old); both kept, the AI guide is the current one.
extracts: When you complete your application, you now have to declare that your personal statement hasn't been copied or provided from another source, including artificial intelligence software.
could in turn mean you don't receive any offers or have offers withdrawn
Copy and paste from AI tools and use as final text. (listed as a don't)
These will then be more detectable through similarity software.

sources.title: UCAS application declaration
UCAS Similarity Detection Service - guidance for applicants (PDF)
sources.notes: 10% threshold for human review. A separate, older UCAS page gives 30% (not stored as its own record because its URL was not returned). Both figures noted, the applicant guide is treated as governing.
extracts: Any statements showing a level of similarity of 10% or more are reviewed by members of the UCAS Similarity Detection Service Team.
If Copycatch finds two sentences in different statements which have exactly the same words, it is very likely that one is a copy of the other
A personal statement which is found to contain copied text may result in the entire application being withdrawn without a refund.

sources.title: Personal statement (LSE undergraduate admissions)
sources.governs: Main statement (LSE is the priority and strictest lens)
sources.notes: Source of the 80% rule, the no-career-in-Q1 rule and equal weight for joint degrees. Disagrees with ucas-3q on future plans in Q1, and with ed-what-you-need on career implications: LSE governs Q1 of the main statement.
extracts: At least 80% of the personal statement should emphasise your interest in the programme, with evidence of critical engagement with the subject and super-curricular activity
Applicants should avoid discussing future career plans in Question 1
Question 3 ... expand on critical reflections already covered in Questions 1 and 2 ... can also hold extra super-curricular activity
Writing only the 350-character minimum for Question 3 is entirely acceptable
give equal weighting to each subject ... a statement weighted towards only one aspect of the programme will be significantly less competitive
our Admissions Selectors will look at how well your academic interests align with the LSE programme
they do not produce high-quality personal statements and may lead to rejection
reserves the right to reject applications where it has been found that a statement has significant similarities to a previous submission or has been created with the use of Artificial Intelligence
generate initial ideas, suggesting reading materials ... and proofreading your own writing (permitted AI uses)

sources.title: Substitute personal statement (section of Durham's personal statement guidance)
sources.notes: Same URL as durham-ps; the substitute guidance is a section of that page. Deadline wording differs between Durham documents (3 days of acknowledgement vs 3 days of UCAS submission); check the applicant portal.
extracts: It is not necessary to write an additional personal statement, however Durham offers a tool for applicants to submit a substitute if the Durham course is very different from the one in the UCAS statement
no more than 4000 characters (including spaces) and plain text, without bold, italics, or underlining

extracts: Social Sciences values independent thought and engagement with reading (search summary of notes)
